name: Anti-communism
summary: Anti-communism is opposition to communism and Soviet-style rule, held by liberals, conservatives, Catholics, social democrats and fascists alike. Mainstream strands defend free markets, private property and elected government against central planning, class struggle and one-party dictatorship, while other strands have backed authoritarian regimes and mass repression in its name.
scope: A composite of the mainstream Cold War Western strand: Truman Doctrine containment, Hayek's critique of planning and Pius XI's Catholic rejection of communism. Anti-communism is a stance that cuts across ideologies, so on issues beyond communism itself the camp is split and many answers are low or 0; the fascist, authoritarian and counter-revolutionary strands are noted but not the centre.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Anti-communists rejected the communist call to turn a war against one's own state, and treated loyalty to the nation against communism as central.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Split: Catholic anti-communists backed moral censorship, while liberal ones defended free expression against totalitarian control.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from the strand's fear of entrenched rulers and its defence of constitutional limits against dictatorship.

recall-officials.rationale: Not an anti-communist question; liberal and conservative anti-communists divided on recall.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The Truman Doctrine commits the US to support free peoples and underlies NATO-style alliances against Soviet expansion.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Pius XI defends private property and Hayek defends markets, so enforced home ownership instead of renting is rejected.

people-in-arms.rationale: Anti-communist states relied on professional armies and the camp has no militia tradition; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The camp spans rural conservatives and urban liberals, so it has no common view.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Cold War anti-communists backed reunifying Germany and Korea under free governments; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Anti-communists generally defended Western civilization against Soviet rule; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Conservative and Cold War anti-communist governments mostly kept capital punishment; the camp is not unanimous.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Pius XI defends parental authority over education against state collectivism; inferred for religious anti-communists.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Pius XI upholds traditional morality and family; inferred lean toward restriction.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Anti-communism cuts across nationalist and liberal strands that disagree on citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: The camp is split between liberals and nationalists on minority language rights.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Pius XI defends religion against hostile state action; inferred sympathy for religious liberty exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Hayek values individual freedom and tradition alike, and other anti-communists lean conformist, so the camp is split.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred: debts are legitimate obligations in the Hayekian and Western liberal view; some Cold War aid did include relief.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the Truman Doctrine's valuing of independence and free institutions as ends in themselves.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream Cold War strand defended existing constitutional order and procedures.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Truman Doctrine contrasts free peoples and free elections with terror and oppression, though some anti-communists backed authoritarian development regimes.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from Cold War aid programmes such as the Truman Doctrine's aid to Greece and Turkey.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred: Western anti-communists generally supported nuclear deterrence, though many relied on alliances.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Split: some anti-communist states elect presidents directly and others use parliaments; the stance does not settle it.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred from Hayek's preference for sound money insulated from political pressure.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Split: the anti-communist camp has no common line on territorial compromise.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Pius XI affirms the social function of property, though liberal anti-communists dissent.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Inferred: mainstream anti-communists and Hayek called Soviet planning socialist and totalitarian rather than capitalist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred: anti-communism is a stance against communism, and market-minded and interventionist strands split on precautionary regulation.

collective-defense.rationale: The Truman Doctrine pledged US support to free peoples resisting Soviet pressure, and Cold War anti-communism was institutionalised in mutual-defence alliances such as NATO.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred: Western anti-communists treated the Soviet annexation of the Baltic states as unlawful and refused to recognise it, though the camp has no single line on annexations generally.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Divini Redemptoris condemns communism for persecuting religion and seizing church property, and anti-communists defend the independence of churches against state control.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: the camp includes republicans, constitutional monarchists and authoritarians, so it has no common view on the head of state's role.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred: containment backed self-determination against Soviet rule, yet anti-communists also fought secessionist movements they saw as communist-led, so the camp is split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Mainstream anti-communism defended constitutional government, separated powers and the rule of law over majority will.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the camp's preference for merit and liberal individualism over state-imposed equality; Catholic strand also opposes it.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Truman and Hayek favour free peoples and open trade; autarkic blocs were a feature of fascist and communist economics.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; the camp is split on whether trade deals should carry standards, with free-market strands against and social democrats in favour.

moral-incentives.rationale: Anti-communists reject the communist call for moral incentives and the abolition of pay in the planned economy; Hayek defends prices and rewards.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Anti-communists reject the vanguard theory of revolution and treat armed revolutionary groups as agents of communist subversion.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not addressed; the Catholic and conservative strand tolerates hereditary order while liberal strands oppose it, so adherents are split but leaning to accept equality before the law.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred: Cold War anti-communists defended Western heritage in education, but liberal anti-communists were split.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from the Truman Doctrine's stress on self-determination; the camp includes colonial-era conservatives, so it is not strong.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred: Cold War anti-communists often wanted schools to teach loyalty against communist subversion, though liberals were wary.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: the camp spans civil-rights liberals and conservatives, so it is split on racial preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: Hayek defends market institutions and sound money against state direction of the economy, so public money creation is rejected.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Anti-communists rejected the Marxist claim that capitalism must collapse, as Hayek's defense of the market order shows.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred: Cold War anti-communists opposed new Soviet influence, but the camp had no single line on old empires.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from the Truman Doctrine's aim of tying free countries to the Western economic order and aid.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Divini Redemptoris and the Truman Doctrine reject the claim that classes have opposed interests, and Western anti-communism held that workers prosper within capitalism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: libertarian anti-communists defend free association, while liberals and Catholics accept anti-discrimination law, so the camp is split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred from Hayek's rule-of-law case for limiting government and the Truman Doctrine's defense of constitutional government.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred: the camp backed self-determination against Soviet domination but never took a common line on colonial borders.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Truman Doctrine sets free elections and representative government against imposed one-party rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: Hayek-style constitutionalism rests on majority rule within limits, with no individual or minority veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: defence of free institutions and rule of law against arbitrary rule, though the camp also included authoritarian strands.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Liberal anti-communists favoured constitutional limits on any legislature while some strands backed monarchs or strongmen, so the camp is split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not an anti-communist question; adherents across liberal, conservative and religious strands differ.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: mainstream Western anti-communists accepted ordinary animal use with welfare limits; the issue was not central.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred: Pius XI calls on the wealthy to practise charity and justice, but liberal and libertarian anti-communists dispute any such duty.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred: the Truman Doctrine and Cold War anti-communism call for active civic and political engagement.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: Hayek and Cold War liberals rejected the Marxist and Frankfurt-style claim that culture pacifies the masses.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The consent-through-culture thesis is a Gramscian Marxist idea that anti-communists generally reject.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: Hayek-style market liberalism holds that trade benefits poor countries rather than extracting their surplus.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not addressed by the camp; liberal strands oppose ethnic offices while nativist and authoritarian strands accept them.

party-own-road.rationale: Anti-communism as such has no position on how other countries run their communist parties, beyond opposing Soviet direction.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The Truman Doctrine is itself a programme of foreign aid, treating it as essential to free peoples resisting communism.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine defends national integrity and the existing order against coercive change.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: free-elections principle and equal citizenship, not rule by descent from earlier peoples.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism as a constitutional value is accepted by some anti-communist strands and rejected by others (some of which were fascist).

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Totalitarian theory equating Nazism and communism is a standard anti-communist position, though fascist strands disagree.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: mainstream Cold War anti-communists accepted the standard history, though neo-Confederate strands dissent.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not an anti-communist question; conservative strands favour preservation while liberal ones are split.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; adherents across the spectrum differ.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed; adherents across the spectrum differ.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred: the Truman Doctrine presents free institutions as the universal choice of free peoples.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Mainstream strands insist on civilian control, but some anti-communist regimes gave the military a guardian role.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: Hayek-style market liberalism and Catholic family doctrine do not favour wages for domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; anti-communists range from religious conservatives to liberals on family obligation.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: Cold War anti-communism defended elected government against appointed party cadres, so rule by examination is not endorsed.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred: the dominant free-market strand, shown in Hayek, favours open ownership, though some strands accept security limits.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Split: the Catholic strand of Divini Redemptoris defends marriage's permanence, while liberal anti-communists accept easy divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: mainstream anti-communism defends representative government and rejects the council and soviet model of recall.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Split: free-market anti-communists favour private accounts, while social-democratic ones back state pensions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Truman Doctrine and Divini Redemptoris defend private property against collectivisation, which covers land held by the community.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Truman Doctrine defends free elected government, which implies legislative control of spending.

single-official-language.rationale: Not addressed; anti-communism cuts across both language-unifying and pluralist positions.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the camp is split on foreign property ownership.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: liberal and conservative anti-communists generally hold discrimination to mean unequal treatment and reject outcome tests.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred: Western consumer abundance was held up as the answer to Soviet scarcity, though Catholic strands criticise materialism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred: the Truman Doctrine pledged support to free peoples resisting armed minorities, and Cold War practice extended to arming anti-communist rebels.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred: mainstream anti-communists condemned Soviet intervention in allied states such as Hungary in 1956, which they saw as aggression.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream Cold War strand defends business and free markets and does not treat lobbying as a threat.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the strand's concern with foreign subversion; Cold War governments did restrict foreign-backed bodies.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Pius XI's encyclical defends the family and a social order built on it; state support for families is inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the defence of private property and free markets.

job-guarantee.rationale: Hayek holds that jobs come from the market and that state direction of labour leads towards planning.

democratic-peace.rationale: The Truman Doctrine backs free peoples and free elections; the idea that democracy brings peace is inferred from it.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Pius XI teaches that authority comes from God and should be obeyed; the strand defends law and order against revolution.

non-intervention.rationale: The Truman Doctrine commits the US to support free peoples against pressure from outside, which is intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: Catholic and liberal anti-communists favoured corporatist or free unions over communist-led industrial unions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A fascist strand blamed 'Judeo-Bolshevism', but the mainstream strand did not, so the answer follows the mainstream.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Pius XI's encyclical defends marriage and the family against communist attacks on them.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the defence of free institutions against one-party secrecy.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from Hayek's case for markets and the price system across distances.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: the strand defends lasting institutions such as church, parties and unions against revolutionary cells.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Atlanticists favour international bodies while sovereigntist anti-communists do not; the camp is split.

religious-nation.rationale: Inferred: the strand defends free peoples of any faith against communist rule; religion is not what defines the nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: Truman Doctrine anti-communism backed self-determination and free peoples, though it also accepted American leadership of the bloc.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Anti-communism is a cross-cutting stance; Hayekian strands favour decentralisation while Catholic and social-democratic strands accept solidarity transfers.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Divini Redemptoris and Hayek defend private property including productive property, so the split between personal goods and common production is rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Opposition to communism as a threat to be resisted and defeated is the defining position, as in the Truman Doctrine and Pius XI.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream Western strand and Hayek accepted a publicly funded safety net run with private and independent providers, though strands differ.

religion-illusion.rationale: Divini Redemptoris condemns the Marxist view of religion, and Cold War anti-communism commonly defended religious faith against atheist rule.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred: Hayek and the Western Cold War strand credit markets with wealth creation, but Catholic and conservative strands criticise capitalism as well.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-communists rejected the Marxist claim that equality needs a changed economic system; Pius XI defended the traditional family and Hayek favoured equality under the law.

socialized-care.rationale: Divini Redemptoris objects to collectivist assaults on family responsibility, and the Western strand rejected state replacement of family care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: language purism is not part of the stance and mainstream liberal and Catholic strands did not pursue it, though some authoritarian strands did.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from the Western strand's stress on law and keeping commitments, though the stance did not address treaties with internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Common property in self-governing communes is a form of the collectivism that Pius XI and Hayek rejected.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream Western strand favoured free elections and self-determination, which cuts against steering majority settlement into minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Catholic and corporatist strands in Divini Redemptoris seek a third way, while Hayek and the liberal strand back capitalism; adherents split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not a question of anti-communism; the camp spans liberals, Catholics, nationalists and others with differing views.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: no anti-communist strand denied the Holocaust, and Cold War anti-communists condemned Nazi crimes; the sources do not discuss it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The camp is split: conservative and Catholic anti-communists often favoured it, while liberal ones did not.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Truman set free elections against terror, so mainstream anti-communism opposes suppression of opposition, though authoritarian strands did it.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Catholic anti-communists like Pius XI favoured religious order, while liberal ones backed religious freedom, so the camp is split.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Truman backed self-determination for free peoples, though some anti-communist regimes ran colonies; the answer is inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; anti-communists generally opposed Soviet-aligned militancy but the statement concerns Muslim duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from Truman's stress on free elections and lawful government, which rejects force against rulers; Catholic strands differ.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred: Hayek's critique of planning favours dispersed decisions in markets, but mainstream anti-communism favours representative government over direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Pius XI rejects class struggle as a frame, so a view that all oppressions overlap is rejected; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anti-communists are split on social questions like this one.

assisted-dying.rationale: The camp is split between religious conservatives and liberals.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Anti-communism cuts across left and right, so adherents see the left-right division as real but not one they share.

alienated-labor.rationale: Pius XI rejects Marxist accounts of capitalism and the class struggle, and Hayek defends markets, so the alienation claim is disputed.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: the camp is split, but mainstream Cold War strands did not treat Islam as a core issue, and the answer leans mildly negative.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Pius XI says authority comes from God while Truman's liberal strand grounds it in the people, so the camp is split.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not an anti-communist question; liberals and conservatives in the camp divide on it.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; the camp divides between business conservatives and liberals.

social-market-economy.rationale: Hayek accepts a safety net and competition rules alongside markets while rejecting planning, and Catholic and social-democratic anti-communists backed social protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Truman Doctrine backed armed support for free peoples, so mainstream anti-communism rejects abolishing armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from Hayek's view of markets as an evolving order, but the camp has no view on staged growth.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Truman Doctrine led the West into blocs such as NATO to contain communism, so staying out of blocs is rejected.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Anti-communism is a stance that cuts across ideologies; the mainstream Cold War strand defended elected government, so hereditary succession is inferred to be rejected.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Hayek and the mainstream strand defend profit-based private banking; the issue is not discussed in the sources, so this is inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Mainstream Western anti-communists backed international lending and market discipline; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: The Truman Doctrine stressed free elections and self-determination, which does not fit a wealth test for voting.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not a concern of the strand; its liberal and conservative adherents would reject the connection, so disagreement is inferred.

reification.rationale: Hayek's critique argues that markets coordinate people's decisions rather than concealing a domination by things; the Marxist concept is rejected.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The mainstream strand held that free elections and a free press under private ownership are real freedoms, in contrast to communist control of the press.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Hayek argued that government must act under general, announced rules, in contrast to arbitrary planning by decree.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Truman Doctrine defended free elections and self-determination, which do not fit a racial test, though authoritarian strands differ.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by the sources; no clear inference.

open-government-data.rationale: Opposition to secretive one-party rule implies support for transparency, but the sources do not discuss open data; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The mainstream strand defended religious freedom against state atheism, so legal limits on interfaith marriage are inferred to be rejected.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The mainstream strand defended religious freedom and tolerance; inferred rejection, though some strands differ.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Never addressed; the camp is split between liberals who favour broad participation and conservative, authoritarian strands that distrust it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Split: Catholic anti-communism as in Divini Redemptoris upholds settled doctrine, while liberal and secular anti-communists take no position on reinterpreting religion.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Hayek and other liberal anti-communists held that concentrated power, including concentrated economic power, threatens liberty, but the camp is mixed on wealth; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anti-communism is not a view on this; liberal and conservative anti-communists divided on it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Pius XI condemned communism as atheistic, and Truman presented Soviet-style rule as a threat to religious freedom, so state-imposed atheism is the thing opposed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The camp defended law, order and national security against subversion, so abolishing police and prisons is rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The camp has no common view on consociational government; liberals, conservatives and Catholics differ.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Catholic subsidiarity and Hayek's preference for voluntary and local action favour private help, though many anti-communists backed welfare programs.

term-limits.rationale: The 22nd Amendment came from the era's fear of concentrated executive power, and the camp's emphasis on limited government points that way; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Anti-communists defended representative government, so permanent revocable delegation of votes is not an established position; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The camp is split and the sources do not address extinction risk, though Cold War anti-communists did prioritise nuclear threats.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Catholic anti-communists opposed it, while liberal and secular strands accepted it, so the camp is split.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Pius XI upheld male headship in the family while secular and liberal anti-communists did not, so the camp is split.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Anti-communism is a stance shared by camps that differ on immigration and local rights, so the camp is split.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from Hayek's case that price controls distort markets, though social-democratic anti-communists accepted rent regulation.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the defence of private property in the Hayek strand, though liberal anti-communists were split on intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: mainstream anti-communists condemned state-run mass youth organisations as Soviet-style indoctrination.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred: the Cold War strand relied on nuclear deterrence, including US weapons based in allied countries.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The Truman Doctrine supported alliances and US presence to defend free peoples, so hosting allied bases was the mainstream position.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: anti-communist movements pressed for recognition of Soviet-era mass killings such as the Holodomor, though the strand did not state a general rule.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the Hayek strand defends returns to capital, though Catholic and social-democratic strands accepted work-based claims.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: mainstream Cold War anti-communism treated armed defence of free peoples as just, and the camp had no pacifist strand.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Never addressed: the camp spans nationalists and liberals who answer differently.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: Divini Redemptoris defends the natural family and the traditional order against communism, which sits against a constructed sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: the Catholic and conservative strands treat women as a fixed category in the family order.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Split: some strands honoured the victims of communism as martyrs, but liberal strands did not use the language of saints.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Divini Redemptoris frames communism as a satanic evil and Truman framed the contest as one of ways of life, so the struggle is moral and spiritual.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Never addressed: the camp has no diaspora doctrine.

culture-before-state.rationale: Never addressed: the camp is a stance against communism, not a nation-building programme.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred: the Catholic strand of the camp speaks of God in traditional male terms.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: the Catholic strand judges texts by the tradition, not by a feminist test.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: the Hayek strand favours open markets and equal treatment, though the authoritarian strands differed.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Never addressed: the camp has no doctrine on regional boundaries.

independent-unions.rationale: Anti-communists held that Soviet-style unions were state-controlled transmission belts, and Cold War Western policy and Catholic teaching defended free, independent unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: anti-communists rejected the claim that Soviet-style rule was socialist in the workers' name, but the statement's framing is Marxist and the camp does not take it up.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not an anti-communist question; liberals and social democrats favoured public utilities while free-market strands wanted them privatised.

second-chamber.rationale: The camp is split on constitutional design; Western anti-communists lived under both bicameral and unicameral systems and it is not part of the stance.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from the defence of private property in Hayek and Divini Redemptoris; communal ownership of production is the kind of collectivism they opposed.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed; inferred only that the stance has no position on municipal federation, and the camp spans centralists and federalists.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from Divini Redemptoris, which says Catholic social teaching requires wages sufficient to support a worker and his family, though liberal and free-market strands did not stress it.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not an anti-communist question; the camp spans free-market deregulators and cautious regulators.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by the stance; adherents are split between market-led and state-funded research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from Hayek's distrust of state control over money and the individual's sphere, though many anti-communists backed financial surveillance against subversion.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed directly; Cold War anti-communists were split between civil-liberties defenders and those who backed surveillance of suspected communists.

person-over-state.rationale: Divini Redemptoris and Hayek both condemn communism for treating the person as a mere instrument of the collective, and the Truman Doctrine framed the contest as free individuals against totalitarian states.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Divini Redemptoris attacks communism as materialist and atheistic, and Cold War anti-communism often cast the struggle as a defence of religion; secular liberal strands did not stress it.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not an anti-communist question; the camp includes federalists and unitarists.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed by the stance; no common position among adherents.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed by the stance; no common position among adherents.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream strand defended individual rights and universalism against collective class or group identity, though fascist strands dissented.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream strand; adherents are split and some strands were racialist while others were universalist.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred: the Truman Doctrine and containment explicitly committed the US to support free peoples against external pressure and so to more than strictly defensive force.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Not an anti-communist question; the camp spans civic nationalists, Catholics and liberals who disagree on what makes a nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: Cold War liberal and Hayekian anti-communists favoured one citizen, one vote, though some Catholic and sectarian systems used communal representation.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Anti-communists saw Soviet-backed subversion and pressure on free peoples as a real threat, as the Truman Doctrine argues, though 'partition' is specific and not the usual framing.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred: free-market and conservative anti-communists generally opposed tuition-free college, while liberal and social-democratic ones supported public education.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Hayekian anti-communism distrusts central direction, though some market-minded anti-communists accept price-based pollution taxes; the camp is split and leans against.

future-generations.rationale: Not an anti-communist question; the camp ranges from conservatives to liberals and environmental views divide.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not an anti-communist question; the camp has no view on gendered values and adherents are split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Containment rested on military strength and the Truman Doctrine backed arming free peoples, so disarmament was resisted while the Soviet threat lasted.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Wilsonian liberals favoured open diplomacy while Cold War practice used secret alliances and covert action, so the camp is split.

capital-controls.rationale: Hayek and Western anti-communists defended free markets against central planning; capital controls were associated with planned economies, though some accepted them in wartime.

missingStatements.text: A government may outlaw political parties that seek to abolish its constitutional order.
missingStatements.rationale: Anti-communist governments banned communist parties and barred their members from public jobs, as in the Hatch Act, Red Purge and West Germany.

notes: Anti-communism is better described as a stance than a full ideology, so salience may be thin. Authoritarian strands (Franco, Pinochet-era, White movement) would answer democracy, violence and civil-liberty items very differently.
